newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - March 11.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - March 11.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Upmarket retailer David Jones Ltd said on Monday that chief executive officer Chris Tideman had resigned, effective immediately, citing personal reasons. A company spokeswoman said David Jones had someone in mind to replace Tideman but would not yet reveal the name.
Davids Ltd is expected to post a first half net profit of A$29 million to A$30 million later on Tuesday, down from A$30.5 million pre-abnormals a year earlier.
Ashton is expected to post a A$30 million net profit for the 1996 year later on Tuesday, up from a net A$21.4 million before abnormals a year earlier.

Baking and milling group Defiance Mills Ltd on Monday repeated its statement that the proposed takeover offer by Bunge Corp was too low. "Defiance Mills' directors are of the view that Bunge's proposed offers fall far short of the true value of the company," Defiance said after a board meeting on Monday.

MIM Holdings Ltd said deliveries of copper and zinc concentrate and lead bullion will resume immediately following the opening of road links between Mt Isa and the port of Townsville in north Queensland. MIM's deliveries of its Mt Isa metals production were stopped late last week when both rail and road links were cut by flood waters following torrential rain caused by severe cyclonic low pressures.

Gaming machine maker AWA Ltd said late on Monday it was looking to expand its business after reporting a A$15.69 million loss for the 1996/97 first half, including a A$21.94 million abnormal loss from the sale of its communications businesses to Plessey Corp.

Metway Bank Ltd said late on Monday business volumes in January and February were pleasing and that it was optimistic about a solid second-half result. Earlier on Monday, Metway reported a 121 percent rise in operating profit for the half to A$73 million and a net profit of A$34 million. There was an pre-tax abnormal loss of A$23 million from write-off costs of a discontinued software project.
